subject: Q4 short pilot: dedicated slice reserve & autoscale exception request
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 short pilot: dedicated slice reserve & autoscale exception request

Team —

Quick ask as we firm up the Acme Health pilot (DEAL-ACME-2198): product would like a short, guaranteed dedicated slice for an end-to-end latency test and integrated A/B for our caching/batching optimizations. Their preferred window is Oct 12–31 (3 weeks).

What we need from infra/ops: a temporary non-preemptible carve of 24 A100 GPUs (or equivalent) for the window, and an autoscale policy exception so the canary and QA traffic won’t be evicted mid-run. We know this is non-trivial given Q4 forecasts, so I’m proposing a 2-tier approach in the attached workbook: 1) guaranteed baseline, 2) burst buffer.

Attachments: q4-dedicated-request.xlsx (proposal + timeline), capacity-delta-diagram.png

Can you confirm whether: 
- We can hold the requested slice (24 A100 equiv) for Oct 12–31?
- If not, what a viable guaranteed + burst split looks like (numbers + SLOs)?
- Any gating (maintenance windows, marketplace pilots) we need to honor so Acme’s run isn’t impacted?

Laura — if infra can’t fully guarantee 24, product needs to know now to set expectations with the customer and adjust the MAP in HubSpot.

Thanks —
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Solutions (Dedicated Capacity)
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 short pilot: dedicated slice reserve & autoscale exception request

Nikhil —

Thanks for the write-up and the workbook. Quick read-through notes:

- We’re tight on A100 headroom in the Oct 10–20 ramp; guaranteed non-preemptible 24 A100s across the entire org is unlikely without displacing current pilots.
- We can offer a firm guarantee on a smaller slice, and then a burst lane that’s probabilistic based on spare capacity. The key operational ask from my side is a clear SLO for preemption/backfill and a defined fallback policy (which model variant to route to).
- If product is ok with a hybrid (guarantee + burst), we’ll need a signed mutual action plan that lists the exact timing for the canary ramp and the telemetry hooks we require to abort on signal.

I’ve cc’d Markus for the exact capacity math and the safest minimal guarantee we can make without impacting other commitments.

- Olga
Senior Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 short pilot: dedicated slice reserve & autoscale exception request

Olga / Nikhil —

After running the headroom and fairness model against the current Q4 commitments (internal + marketplace), here’s what I can commit to today: 

1) Firm guarantee: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs for the full Oct 12–31 window, non-preemptible.
2) Burst buffer: entitlement to request up to an additional 12 A100-equivalent GPUs subject to availability; burst requests will be handled via our burst queue and are preemptible if higher-priority commitments occur.
3) Autoscale exception: we can allow a temporary override for the canary window (Oct 12–16) to prevent eviction, but it must be timeboxed and require explicit telemetry signals to revoke.

Operational constraints / asks: 
- We need a signed MAP with exact ramp steps and abort criteria (error rate, latency degradation, token-cost delta).
- No marketplace pilots that increase A100 demand will be accepted during Oct 12–16 without prior approval from capacity stewardship.
- Product must expose telemetry hooks (latency, 5xx rates, queue depth) to the ops team in real time.

If product accepts (12 + 12 burst) we’ll draft the reservation and ingress rules. If Acme insists on a hard 24 guaranteed, we’ll need to bump their contract tier (cost + lead time) or shift other pilots.

-Markus
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 short pilot: dedicated slice reserve & autoscale exception request

Thanks Markus — this compromise is workable for product and Acme, provided we lock the canary exception and get the MAP updated.

Action items I’ll take: 
- Laura, please update the HubSpot MAP (HS-98765) to reflect 12 guaranteed + 12 burst and the Oct 12–31 window; include the abort criteria Markus listed.
- I’ll attach the signed MAP to the reservation paperwork and loop procurement for PO timing.
- Ops, once the MAP is final, please generate the reservation ticket and the ingress rules (INF-721).

I’ve added the updated workbook with a second tab that outlines the reduced guarantee plus burst flow. If you can review by EOD, we’ll share the updated plan with Acme.

Thanks —
Nikhil
Head of Solutions (Dedicated Capacity)
Redwood Inference
